analysis.title: Fed holds rates steady despite inflation being too high
key_insights: The Fed voted 10-2 to hold the Fed funds target range at 3.75%-4%. Only 2bp of a 25bp hike was priced beforehand and only 6 of 97 organisations polled by Bloomberg predicted a hike, so market reaction was limited.

Beth Hammack and Lisa Cook dissented in favour of a further hike. Cook's dissent was a surprise given her reputation as a centrist. ING had expected Kashkari and/or Logan, who both dissented in July, to join Hammack.
The press release was little changed: the economy is 'expanding at a strong pace' and 'inflation remains elevated'. It made no pre-commitment to further action and tied policy to data.

Chair Warsh gave no real guidance beyond saying inflation remains too high. He said the overwhelming consensus in the FOMC is that the 'medicine' is starting to work and that the Fed will deliver price stability, 'no ifs, ands or buts'.
From next September one FOMC meeting will have no rate vote and will focus on monetary policy strategy. From 2028 this becomes two meetings, leaving six meetings with rate decisions.

ING's base case is a December 2026 hike to 4.00%-4.25%. Two jobs reports and one inflation print come before the decision, and November CPI is released the day after the Fed meeting, so officials will see it before the market does.
ING's forecast path assumes that in the months after the midterm elections an agreement improves energy flow from the Persian Gulf and sharply cuts shipping and insurance costs, lowering pump prices.

ING expects US inflation to fall to 2% in 2H 2027, helped by wage growth of 3% and further disinflation in housing (35% of the inflation basket). It forecasts a prolonged pause through December 2027, when the December 2026 hike is reversed.
The Fed's own projections show one hike this year and no change through 2027. ING's path matches the current consensus forecast.

The 10-year Treasury yield had been holding at 4.99% before the meeting. ING sees the hawkish-leaning statement as validating a move back above 5% and keeps its view of a path toward 5.25%. The yield briefly dipped below 5% during the press conference on Warsh's comments that inflation expectations had been tamed somewhat, but inflation expectations rose after the decision.

The implementation note was unchanged. The Fed keeps reinvesting MBS principal payments into Treasury bills. A balance sheet shrinkage plan is still some way off, with committee recommendations expected near the turn of the year. Repo is behaving much better than a year ago.

The dollar softened slightly, which ING attributes to positioning after a one-way run higher since early September driven by energy prices, solid US activity and French budget concerns. ING does not think the dollar needs to correct much and expects consolidation near the top of recent ranges unless the ECB (Thursday) or BOJ (Friday) surprise hawkishly.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Held by a 10-2 vote, with two dissents in favour of a hike.

macro_indicators.indicator: Fed funds target range (ING forecast, December 2026)
macro_indicators.interpretation: ING expects a 25bp hike in December, reversed by December 2027.
A majority of FOMC members project a hike before year-end.
ING expects inflation to return to target on lower energy costs and housing disinflation.
Benign wage growth is the biggest corporate cost input and supports disinflation.
ING sees the yield back above 5% heading toward 5.25%.

risk_factors: November CPI is released the day after the December FOMC meeting. Officials will see it first, so a market surprise cannot be ruled out.
The Persian Gulf energy and shipping agreement in ING's base case may not materialise, which would keep pump prices and inflation higher.
Higher Treasury yields and a firmer dollar are tightening financial conditions.
Inflation expectations rose after the Fed decision and Warsh's comments.
A hawkish surprise from the ECB (Thursday) or BOJ (Friday) could disrupt the dollar consolidation view.
vol_and_positioning: The dollar's slight softening after the Fed is attributed to positioning following a one-way run higher since early September.
geopolitical: An agreement after the US midterm elections to improve energy flow from the Persian Gulf and reduce shipping and insurance costs is assumed in ING's Fed path.
French budget woes are cited as a driver of dollar strength since early September.
The relationship between Lisa Cook and President Trump is described as fraught.

tension_points.bull_case: A majority of FOMC members project a hike before year-end and ING sees a December hike as a solid bet, with Warsh insisting on strict 2% price stability.
tension_points.bear_case: The Fed held in October and gave no forward guidance. Officials like Jefferson, Bowman and Waller see little need for back-to-back hikes, and Warsh said the 'medicine' is starting to work.
tension_points.what_invalidates: November CPI, released the day after the December FOMC meeting and seen by officials before the market, could surprise and change the decision.

theme_stances.key_argument: A December hike looks a solid bet given a majority of FOMC members project a hike this year and inflation remains too high.
theme_stances.evidence: a December hike looks a solid bet

theme_stances.key_argument: The hawkish-leaning statement and rising inflation expectations validate the move back above 5% on the 10yr.
theme_stances.evidence: enough to validate the move back above 5% on the 10yr

theme_stances.key_argument: Strong US growth and above-target inflation mean the dollar does not need to correct much.
theme_stances.evidence: the dollar does not need to correct much at all
